text: Motion (version 1): The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on every repository.
label: opening

text: I used Lintwise daily for six months on my previous team. It caught real bugs—null dereferences, off-by-one errors—that would have shipped otherwise. That value is genuine. My one concern is CI time: adding four minutes to our eleven-minute build pushes us to roughly fifteen minutes per PR, which is a noticeable drag on an eight-person team sharing one monorepo. I'd vote for this motion, but I want us to scope Lintwise to changed files rather than the full repo, and to run it in parallel with the existing build steps instead of sequentially. If we can keep the wall-clock increase under two minutes, the tradeoff is clearly worth it. If we can't, we should revisit after a one-month trial.
tldr: Lintwise caught real bugs for me; I support it but want parallel execution and changed-files-only scoping to limit CI impact.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: I own the pipeline, and 11 minutes is already the number everyone complains about when queue depth spikes at 2 PM. Adding a mandatory gate to every repo in a monorepo means every branch, every commit, pays a tax. If Lintwise runs in under 15 seconds, fine, I'll slot it as a parallel job next to the build and it's invisible. If it's 90 seconds or more, I'm now pushing every developer's feedback loop past 12 minutes and my queue grows. I also need to know: does it block on warnings or only errors? A false-positive flood will have people pinging me at midnight to bypass the check, and then the gate is theater. Before I sign off, I want a one-week shadow run on the monorepo so I can see actual wall-clock cost and flake rate.
tldr: I'll support Lintwise only if a shadow run proves it adds under 15 seconds and produces near-zero false positives.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: As a security engineer, I favor any pre-merge gate that blocks bad code before it reaches main. However, "code-quality checker" is vague. My concern: does Lintwise actually detect hardcoded secrets, insecure API usage, or vulnerable dependency patterns, or is it primarily style and naming? If it's just formatting, it won't reduce my risk surface. I also worry about CI time—our builds already average 11 minutes; adding another required check without measuring its runtime could push us past acceptable thresholds and tempt developers to bypass the pipeline. I'd support adoption only if we first verify Lintwise's rule set covers secret-detection and dependency advisories, and confirm it adds no more than 60 seconds to the pipeline. Otherwise we get compliance theater, not security.
tldr: Support adoption only if Lintwise's rules cover secrets and dependency risk, and it adds minimal CI time.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: I've run Lintwise on a side project for a few weeks, and it caught real issues—unused imports, inconsistent async patterns, a few subtle bugs I'd have shipped. As the person touching most of the JS in our monorepo, I'd welcome the consistency. My one concern is CI time: we're already at 11 minutes per build. If Lintwise adds more than a minute or two, we'll feel it on every push. I'd support making it required, but I'd ask that we run it as a parallel job rather than a sequential gate, and that we give ourselves a two-week grace period to fix existing violations before the check actually blocks merges. Otherwise we'll have a wall of red on day one and people will start ignoring it.
tldr: Used Lintwise; it catches real bugs. Support it as required, but run in parallel and allow a grace period for existing violations.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: I haven't touched Lintwise, so I can't speak to its rule quality. What I *can* flag: my pipelines are roughly 60% SQL and 40% Python orchestration. If Lintwise is primarily a Python/JS tool, it may either skip my SQL entirely or throw false positives on dialect-specific syntax I use daily. That's a lot of noise for a "required" gate. Also, our CI already averages eleven minutes; I'd want a measured latency number before making it mandatory. I'm not opposed in principle—cleaner Python in the pipeline code would help—but "required on every repo" before I've seen its output on my SQL feels premature. I'd support a two-week opt-in trial on the data-pipelines directory first, so I can judge whether it catches real issues or just adds friction.
tldr: Undecided—need SQL-coverage evidence and a CI-latency number before endorsing a mandatory gate.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: I support this, with conditions. As QA lead, my priority is that every signal in CI is trustworthy. A static checker that catches style and correctness issues before merge reduces the noise I see in test failures caused by preventable defects. However, I need two things: first, a strict rule set with zero default warnings that aren't actionable—every finding must either block or be explicitly suppressed by a reviewer, never silently ignored. Second, the check must run in under 90 seconds so we don't bloat the 11-minute CI window. If Lintwise emits false positives at a rate above roughly 5%, developers will start dismissing it, and we lose the signal. I'll help curate the initial ruleset to keep it tight.
tldr: Support adoption if the ruleset is strict, fast, and free of ignorable noise.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: I'm in favor, with one condition. As the person who owns our merge policy, I've watched style drift creep into the monorepo over the last two quarters—three separate PRs last month had inconsistent error-handling patterns that only surfaced at review. A static checker at the gate catches that before a human spends twenty minutes flagging it. However, our CI already averages eleven minutes. If Lintwise adds more than ninety seconds to that pipeline, I'll block the rollout until we can parallelize it with the build. I want the check enforced, but I want it fast enough that no one starts gaming the process by pushing untested branches at 5 PM. Let's set a hard time budget for the lint step and revisit in two sprints.
tldr: Adopt Lintwise as a gate, but cap its runtime so the eleven-minute CI budget doesn't slip.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: Honestly, as someone still learning our conventions, I think this could really help me. Right now I sometimes get style feedback only during review, which feels slow and sometimes discouraging. If Lintwise catches formatting or style issues before a human even looks at my PR, I can fix things myself without waiting for a senior teammate to notice. I haven't used Lintwise yet, so I'd appreciate a quick onboarding doc or a short walkthrough so I understand what it flags and how to configure it locally. My one concern is whether the rules are already tuned to our monorepo or if we'll spend the first week fighting false positives. But overall, I'd rather have a consistent, automated baseline than rely on tribal knowledge I haven't absorbed yet.
tldr: As a junior dev, automated style checks give me clearer guidance than waiting on review comments.
label: round 1 (blind)

text: To Priya: Measured wall-clock runtime and false-positive rate of Lintwise during six months of daily use (I need concrete numbers: how many seconds did Lintwise typically take on a changed-files run versus a full-repo run, and roughly what percentage of its findings turned out to be false positives that required a manual suppress or ignore comment?)
label: fact-finding question

text: Full-repo run: roughly four minutes. With result cache enabled—which effectively skips unchanged files, approximating a changed-files run—it dropped to about one minute. I don't have a precise false-positive percentage from my notes. I recall it caught three null-handling bugs in month one, and most findings were actionable. I'd need to check my old suppress-comment count to give you a real FP rate.
tldr: Four minutes full-repo, one minute cached; I lack a measured false-positive percentage and won't guess one.
label: answer to chair

text: To Marcus: Current CI infrastructure's ability to run a parallel lint job alongside the 11-minute build (Can you confirm whether the existing CI runners have spare capacity to launch Lintwise as a parallel job next to the build step without increasing queue wait time, and what the current peak queue depth looks like around 2 PM?)
label: fact-finding question

text: Peak queue wait is already six minutes—builds average eleven, so developers see roughly seventeen minutes before green. I haven't measured Lintwise myself; the four-minute figure is Priya's. I can't confirm spare runner capacity for a parallel job without a load test. Adding even one minute to queue at peak compounds the 2 PM pileup. I need a one-week shadow run before I can answer this honestly.
tldr: Peak queue is six minutes; I can't confirm parallel capacity without a measured shadow run.
label: answer to chair

text: The motion is clear, but I still lack a measured false-positive percentage from my six months of use, and Marcus and Sana have both conditioned their support on concrete data (shadow-run timing under 15 s, SQL-coverage evidence, parallel-capacity confirmation) that none of us can supply from memory; running a short shadow run on our monorepo to capture wall-clock time, FP rate, and coverage gaps before the vote would let everyone decide on facts rather than caveats.
label: needs time to research

text: I need a measured shadow run on our actual monorepo to confirm Lintwise adds under 15 seconds in parallel and to verify parallel capacity at peak queue, because without that data I cannot responsibly endorse a mandatory gate that could push our 11-minute builds and 6-minute queues further.
label: needs time to research

text: I would pull Lintwise's published ruleset to confirm it ships secret-detection patterns (API keys, tokens, private keys) and a dependency-vulnerability check before I can endorse a mandatory gate, because without verified coverage of those two areas the tool does not serve the security purpose I require, and Priya's admitted lack of a false-positive rate compounds the risk of noisy security rules being ignored.
label: needs time to research

text: I would look into whether Lintwise's rule set actually parses and checks .sql files (the format of my pipeline code) and run a timed shadow check on one of my SQL-heavy pipeline repos to measure the added latency against my specific workload, because without confirming SQL coverage the gate is a no-op for my code, and without a repo-specific latency number I cannot tell whether the four-minute figure Priya cited applies to my pipelines or whether it would push my CI past an acceptable threshold.
label: needs time to research

text: I would look into the measured false-positive rate per rule category (via a one-week shadow run on the monorepo) because my core acceptance criterion is "free of ignorable noise," and Priya explicitly stated she has no FP percentage to cite, so I cannot judge signal-to-noise without that number.
label: needs time to research

text: Before voting to make Lintwise a mandatory gate, I would run a shadow pass on the monorepo to measure its actual wall-clock contribution (target: under 15 s on changed files) and its false-positive rate, because Marcus and Sana both withhold support without those numbers and I won't lock in a required check that could push our 11-minute CI budget past tolerance without hard data.
label: needs time to research

text: I'd want to see the shadow-run results Marcus and Sana are asking for—specifically the measured false-positive rate and actual added CI seconds—because as a junior dev I need the checker to give me clear, trustworthy guidance rather than noisy or wrong feedback that could confuse me more than a human review comment would.
label: needs time to research

text: Motion tabled to the next meeting. Research: Priya: Pull old suppress-comment count from six-month Lintwise usage to produce a concrete false-positive percentage per rule category. | Marcus: Run a one-week shadow pass on the monorepo to measure (a) Lintwise wall-clock time on changed files, (b) whether existing CI runners have spare capacity to launch it as a parallel job at the 2 PM peak queue, and (c) resulting queue-depth impact. | Elena: Pull Lintwise's published ruleset and confirm it ships secret-detection patterns (API keys, tokens, private keys) and a dependency-vulnerability check; report coverage gaps. | Sana: Run a timed shadow check on one SQL-heavy pipeline repo to confirm Lintwise parses .sql files without dialect false positives and measure added latency against her specific workload. | Lars: Review the shadow-run output for measured false-positive rate per rule category; flag any rule emitting noise above ~5%. | Jin: Aggregate shadow-run wall-clock and FP data; confirm the lint step stays under 15 s in parallel before endorsing a hard merge gate. | Olga: Review shadow-run findings on a sample PR to judge whether the feedback is clear and actionable for a junior dev, or noisy enough to cause confusion.
label: tabled
